normalized.description: Objective:The objective of this study is to investigate the High-throughput Optical Network evolution (HydRON EVO) as the backbonenetwork enabling a total capacity of tens to hundreds TbpsTargeted Improvements:To assess the feasibility of optical space backbone network with total capacity in the range of tens to hundreds TbpsDescription:Following the terrestrial network analogy, backbone (long-haul) networks provide capacity beyond Terabit-per-second (Tbps) per single line (with links beyond 800 Gbps per wavelength). The current HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) demonstration system will demonstrate single-link communications from 2.5G to 100Gbps, addressing both user access and the lower datarate backbone links. To enable growth of optical space networks, as an extension of the terrestrial fibre network, a space backbone is required to support multi-Tbps capacity in space. The backbone should be interoperable and interface with multiple networks like the one developed in HydRON demonstration system. However, using DWDM technologies and commercial coherent transceivers, the single link capacity can be increased beyond Tbps, and by aggregating multiple channels the network capacity can be increased to tens or even hundreds Tbps.This activity shall address the design and technology trade-offs of a space network backbone exceeding several Tbps and serving other space networks. It shall provide a set of requirements and a system concept. It shall be verified by analysis that the system concept is scalable at higher rates. Interoperability aspects shall be analysed, to guarantee the connectivity among networks (including terrestrial fibre networks). Technology gaps shall be identified and technology roadmap provided. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technologyas well as the operational concept can be demonstrated, to further push the technology borders in terms of data rates/capacity aiming to maintain the strategic leadership position of the Europen/Canadian Industry The activity will also contribute to the evolutionof ESTOL.
